# ADR-0158 — Dark mode ships, and the ink a surface carries becomes a token

**Status:** Accepted (designed 2026-08-02, session 209) — design accepted; the build is phased in §10 and tracked in [backlog.md](../backlog.md).
**Design reference:** [`mockups/dark-mode-v1.html`](../../mockups/dark-mode-v1.html), generated by `mockups/build-dark-mode-v1.mjs` from the app's real CSS and DOM captured from the running app.
**Builds on:** [0028](0028-plan-violet-color-budget-dark-ready.md) (the colour budget, mode identity, and "dark mode is a token remap"), [0082](0082-adopt-non-color-design-tokens.md) (the token layer and the U-08 sweep), [0105](0105-loading-states-design.md) (the dark boot, designed and dormant), [0121 §11](0121-embedded-map-phase-6-design.md) (the night map style, authored and inert), [0133 §5/§7](0133-the-user-is-a-surface-identity-ramp-and-a-reachable-roster.md) (the identity ramp; the theme toggle rejected in July).
**Amends:** ADR-0133 §7 (the toggle's rejection expires), ADR-0028 and `design-language.md` (the dark-mode mechanism, and the palette gains four token families).

## Context

Dark mode was **complete and inert**. `tokens.css` carried a full
`:root[data-theme='dark']` remap including all five identity hues; `App.css` and
`screens.css` had been swept onto tokens; both Map IDs existed with the night
style authored; ADR-0105 had designed the dark boot. And **nothing in the tree
ever set `data-theme`**, so across the three weeks of work that accumulated it
(ADR-0028 on 2026-07-12 through the U-08 sweep), the dark theme had never once
been rendered.

This session set it, on the running app, and audited both themes together. Two of
the remap's own recorded conventions turn out to be wrong, the trip chrome turns
out to have an unenumerated dependency on being dark, and — the result nobody was
looking for — **the shipped light theme fails contrast far more often than the
unshipped dark one.**

Measured on the real app across eight routes, both themes, contrast computed per
text node against its composited background:

|                                 | text nodes failing AA         | on-fill ink failing |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------- |
| **light (shipped today)**       | **78 of 238**                 | 0                   |
| **dark (the remap as written)** | 12 of 238, all one root cause | **10 sites**        |

Each theme was hiding the other's bug class. Light was never audited because it
looked fine; dark was never audited because it could not be seen.

## Decision

### 1. The ink a surface carries is a token, named for the surface

Every defect below is one shape: **a token whose value was chosen for one of its
two roles.** `--plan-deep` was remapped as text and used as a fill.
`--amber-deep` was chosen as an accent and used as small text. Twenty-four
literal inks were painted onto fills whose polarity flips. The repo already
solved this once — `--amber-ink` exists precisely because "dark amber text" and
"amber fill" are different jobs — and nobody generalised it.

So the rule, stated once: **when a colour is painted _onto_ something, the ink is
its own token, named for what it sits on.** Four families, all following
`--amber`/`--amber-ink`'s shape and all folding call sites rather than adding
names beside them (rule 8).

### 2. `--on-fill` / `--on-amber` — ink on a semantic fill

`App.css` and `screens.css` both record: _"ink that rides a semantic FILL — the
fill re-maps, the on-fill ink must not."_ That is true for a fill that keeps its
**polarity** (`--amber` is light in both themes, `--indigo` dark in both) and
false for every **mid-tone** one, because those were brightened for text
legibility on dark grounds, which pushes them past the point where white ink
works.

| Site                                            | Fill      | Light | Dark today | Dark fixed |
| ----------------------------------------------- | --------- | ----- | ---------- | ---------- |
| `.choice-pill.on`, `.wp-event-act:hover`        | `--ink`   | 15.65 | **1.20**   | 13.49      |
| `.wp-event-check`, `.bld-settle.done`           | `--ok`    | 3.48  | **2.31**   | 7.03       |
| `.wp-placebadge-mark`, `.wp-event-act.go:hover` | `--teal`  | 3.35  | **2.56**   | 6.34       |
| `.hdr-sync-badge`                               | `--muted` | 4.68  | **2.64**   | 6.16       |
| `.confirm[danger] .confirm-confirm` + 2         | `--miss`  | 4.38  | **2.93**   | 5.55       |
| `.gapfill-new` + 7                              | `--plan`  | 5.17  | 3.50       | 4.64       |

`background: var(--ink); color: #fff` at **1.20:1** is white on near-white, on
`.choice-pill.on` — a selected state in the app's forms.

- **`--on-fill`** — `#FFFFFF` light, `#12203A` dark. This is exactly what
  `--cta-text` already is; `--cta-text` becomes an alias of it. ADR-0028 wrote
  the insight ("CTA is a pair … they flip together") and applied it to one token.
- **`--on-amber`** — `#3A2405` in both themes, for the one fill that is light in
  both.

**What must not join the family:** `--indigo` and the board / land / join
grounds. Those are always-dark **chrome**, so they keep light ink in both themes
— dark ink on dark indigo measures **1.01:1**. Two different rules had been
written down as one, which is how this shipped.

### 3. `--on-dark` — the ink ramp for always-dark surfaces

The larger half of the same fold, and the reason `/login`'s "~21 literals" is the
wrong framing. Across the always-dark surface family — the board, the indigo
chrome, the day strip, `/login`, `/join`, the boarding-pass ticket, the trip
hero, the plan hero, the zero-state head — there are **53 light-ink declarations
carrying 18 distinct hex values, doing three jobs.**

```
bright  #fff #eef2fb #eaf0ff #e4ebf8 #dfe6f5 #dce3f2 #cdd8ef   27 sites, L* 86–100
dim     #c3cee8 #b9c4de #aeb9d4 #9fb0d2 #9daac8 #93a2c4
        #8ea1c6 #8fa0c4 #8494b5                               23 sites, L* 61–83
faint   #7e8fb4 #7688ac                                        3 sites, L* 56–59
```

This is ADR-0082's argument in a different channel: the type ramp drifted to
`11.5/12.5/13.5/15/16/19px` because it lived only in prose, and the fix was to
put the ramp in the CSS. Same here.

**Four tokens, theme-fixed in both themes** (these surfaces are dark in light
mode too, which is the whole point):

| Token              | Value     | Job                        | Folds    |
| ------------------ | --------- | -------------------------- | -------- |
| `--on-dark-strong` | `#FFFFFF` | titles, the loud numeral   | 15 sites |
| `--on-dark`        | `#EAF0FF` | body ink on a dark surface | 12 sites |
| `--on-dark-dim`    | `#93A2C4` | secondary / labels         | 22 sites |
| `--on-dark-faint`  | `#7688AC` | tertiary                   | 3 sites  |

`#93A2C4` is both the modal value (11 uses) and the correct one: the runtime
sweep caught `.wp-daypill .l` at **4.02:1** in light, because the pill's 5% white
wash lightens the ground under `#8494b5`; `#93A2C4` clears it.

**This replaces "mark the ~21 literals `fixed:`" with something better.** A
marker is a comment asserting intent; a token whose name is `--on-dark-dim`
_states_ it, cannot drift, and needs no comment. The `fixed:` convention stays
for what genuinely remains: ink riding a semantic fill (now `--on-fill`), the
Google brand mark, and the light/dark swatches inside §8's theme control — which
are a _picture of the option_, so they are theme-fixed by construction.

**The precedent to generalise is already in the tree:** `ui/zone-shift-pill.css`
has `.wp-tzshift.on-dark` — one component that invented this exact concept for
itself. Rule 8 says generalise that rather than write a second.

### 4. `--plan-surface` — plan's hero is a surface, not an accent

`--plan-deep`'s dark value is `#A99AF2`, commented _"used as text — lighter on
dark"_. It is **also a fill**, at `.prep` (the plan hero) and
`.gapfill-new:hover`. So in dark mode the plan hero renders at **L\* 68 — the
brightest surface in the entire app** — with its own ink at **2.16:1**, in the
mode `design-language.md` calls _calm_, out-shouting the trip board it is meant
to sit below. **This inverts mode identity**, which ADR-0028 makes
non-negotiable.

The root cause is an asymmetry: the trip hero has dedicated surface tokens
(`--board`/`--board-2`) and the plan hero paints itself out of the **accent**
tokens. An accent brightens on dark; a surface must not.

- **`--plan-surface`** `#6E59D6` light / `#2A2158` dark
- **`--plan-surface-2`** `#5747B4` light / `#332866` dark

Light values are byte-identical to the gradient they replace, so light mode does
not move. Dark gives a deep violet night surface — plan's counterpart of the
night board — with ink at **12.7:1**, and it restores the luminance channel the
right way round: **trip is near-black with amber inside it, plan is a lifted
violet slab with white on it.**

### 5. `--chrome-*` — the chrome's contract, so the third copy is never written

Sweeping every colour declaration on a trip-chrome surface finds **53, of which
4 carry a marker**. None is wrong today: each is correct _given a dark chrome_,
and nothing records that dependency. The avatar's ring is
`.av { border: 2px solid var(--indigo) }` — a ring meant to separate overlapping
avatars _on_ the dark bar, which on a light bar is a hard navy outline.

The decisive fact is that **plan mode already solved all of it.** When plan's
chrome went light it re-specified the entire set, and
`.app[data-mode='plan'] .av { border-color: var(--card) }` is literally that
ring. So a light trip chrome (§9) would be the **third** hand-written copy of
"how chrome children look on a given ground" — the shape ADRs
[0078](0078-feedback-state-family.md), [0079](0079-single-modal-primitive.md),
[0094](0094-one-pluggable-change-applier-registry.md) and [0095](0095-named-constants-for-string-discriminants.md) all
exist to undo.

**Six names** (this ADR first said five; the build found the chrome needs a
distinct rung for _numerals_ — the day number and the anchor's value sit a step
above labels and a step below titles), set once per mode, replacing nineteen
hand-written rules:

```
--chrome-bg  --chrome-ink  --chrome-ink-mid  --chrome-ink-num
--chrome-ink-dim  --chrome-ring
```

And a seventh thing that is deliberately **not** a token: the washes. Those run
at eight different alphas across the chrome, so one `--chrome-wash` could only
serve them by folding — which would move pixels for no reason. Instead each
element mixes its own alpha off the ink: `color-mix(in srgb, var(--chrome-ink)
9%, transparent)`. Every existing alpha is preserved exactly, and the wash still
flips with the chrome, because a white wash on dark chrome becomes an ink wash on
a light one with no per-element rule to rewrite.

Trip-dark keeps exactly today's values, so this is a **no-op refactor** on its
own. Plan-light collapses to setting the same five. It is worth doing whether or
not §9 ever ships, because it turns an undocumented dependency into a recorded
one — and it makes §9 seven lines instead of nineteen rules.

### 6. The light theme's own four failures

The reconciliation's real surprise. All are **scalar darkenings along the same
RGB ray**, so hue and saturation are mathematically untouched.

| Token          | Was       | Becomes   | On `--card`     | On `--screen`   |
| -------------- | --------- | --------- | --------------- | --------------- |
| `--muted`      | `#6C7488` | `#61687A` | 4.68 → 5.57     | **3.88** → 4.62 |
| `--amber-deep` | `#C9822A` | `#915E1E` | **3.13** → 5.49 | 2.60 → 4.55     |
| `--faint`      | `#98A0B0` | see §7    | **2.63**        | **2.18**        |

**`--amber` itself is not touched.** The signature amber `#E9A63C` lives on the
dark board at 8.51:1. Only `--amber-deep` — amber's _paper_ variant, carrying
10–12.5px bold times across zone chips, leg badges, the glance rail and the
tz-shift pill — moves. The product's signature colour is unchanged and rule 4's
budget is untouched: the same hue at a legible depth.

Also caught, and **only** by a real render: `.nav` is
`rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.92)`. The U-08 sweep converted _hexes_, so it never looked
at this, and the tab bar stays white in dark mode — which is the single root
cause of **all 12** dark failures in the table above (the nav labels are
`--muted` on white, 2.24:1, on every tab of every screen). Fixing it takes dark
mode to **zero failing text nodes**. It becomes
`color-mix(in srgb, var(--card) 92%, transparent)`, identical in light.

### 7. `--faint` narrows to placeholders, and hints move to `--muted`

The one place the measurement forces a real design choice rather than a value.
`--faint`'s call sites are 11.5–15px normal text, so their floor is AA **4.5**,
not the 3.0 a hint might argue for. Darkening `--faint` to clear 4.5 lands it at
**L\* 44.6** against `--muted`'s **L\* 44.0** — 0.6 apart, visually identical.
**The three-step ink ramp cannot survive AA at small sizes on white.**

Rather than keep a token that must equal its neighbour to be legible, `--faint`
**narrows to what genuinely differs**: a `::placeholder` — transient, replaced by
the user's own text, and the one case where WCAG's text requirement is arguable.
Everything persistent that currently reads `--faint` — `.field-hint`,
`.new-note`, `.set-hint-block`, section hints — moves to `--muted`. Hierarchy
below `--muted` is then carried by **size and weight**, which is more robust than
0.6 L\* of colour anyway.

Dark is unaffected (`--faint` measures 4.76 there) but follows the same narrowing,
because a token means one thing in both themes.

**Amended at build time (phase 5), and the outcome is better than this section
predicted.** The section framed it as a choice between darkening `--faint` and
narrowing it. It is both, and they are not in tension: narrowed to transient
text, `--faint`'s floor is **3.0**, not 4.5 — so it can be deepened to
`#808694` (3.65 on `--card`, 3.03 on `--screen`) and still sit **11.9 L\* below
`--muted`**. The collapse this section feared only happens at a 4.5 floor, which
narrowing removes. So the third step survives _and_ every value clears its
floor; 21 persistent-hint sites moved to `--muted`, and 9 genuinely transient
ones kept `--faint`.

### 8. The toggle: three rungs, on the device, before first paint

ADR-0133 §7 rejected a theme toggle on `/settings` in July for one stated reason
— _"a switch that does nothing is worse than a thin page"_ — which was true while
the remap was inert and **expires the moment it is not.** That rejection is
hereby amended, not overturned: the reason was correct and its condition has
changed.

- **Three rungs — `מערכת` / `בהיר` / `כהה`, `system` by default.** Two rungs
  force a shipped default and a dark-mode phone would open light. `system` is
  also the only honest state for someone who has never chosen, and it must keep
  **tracking**: the stored value is the _pick_, and the resolved theme is
  computed from it plus a live `matchMedia` listener.
- **Stored on the device, and that is the design rather than the shortcut.** The
  theme must be on `<html>` **before first paint** or the app flashes light — a
  server-stored preference structurally cannot beat the first frame, and would
  change the theme _after_ paint. A local store is load-bearing even if a server
  copy existed, so the server copy would be pure duplication with a flash
  attached. It is also the honest model: theme is a property of **the screen you
  are holding** (a phone at night and a laptop in daylight legitimately
  disagree), where `avatarHue` — the stored-preference precedent — is a property
  of the person.
- **Two things that must follow the resolved theme and are easy to miss:**
  `<meta name="theme-color">`, hardcoded `#1B2A4A` today, which paints the
  browser's own chrome bar; and the Map's cloud style, already plumbed
  (`MAP_THEME` + `readMapsConfig(env, theme)`, ADR-0121 §11). The map is safe
  from ADR-0121 §4's no-re-instantiate rule **for free**, because
  `Map.tsx:514` already latches its config in a `useMemo(…, [])` — so a
  mid-visit theme flip cannot construct a second billed map, and the style
  follows on the next tab visit.
- **The dark boot** ships as ADR-0105 drew it: one rule giving `.fb-boot` the
  same `--board-2` → `--board` ground `/login` uses, so boot → login is one
  continuous surface in dark.

### 9. `/login` and `/join` stay theme-fixed; the light trip chrome is deferred

**`/login` and `/join/:token` do not theme.** They are already at the dark end of
the axis — theming them means giving them a light state they have never had, and
the only other reading ("the ground goes a few L\* darker") is what
`--board`/`--board-2` already do for free. They are the same surface class as the
indigo header and the ticket, and §3 gives every one of their inks a name that
says so. ADR-0142's anticipation glow and ADR-0143's perforation and stamp are
choreographed against those grounds and are untouched.

**The light trip chrome is a real question and it is not this ADR's to answer.**
Light mode is ~220px of dark chrome above a dark hero, so it reads half-dark. The
mockup's four renders establish that the **hero is load-bearing** — lighten it
and the chrome inherits the prominence, inverting the hierarchy, because in light
mode darkness is the hero's only prominence mechanism (amber-as-a-ground was
rejected in ADR-0105) — and that the **chrome** is what looks out of place. Four
grounds are drawn and **indigo 12%** recommended, because it keeps the trip hue
so mode identity survives on hue rather than luminance.

Deferred, deliberately, with the reasons recorded: it moves a surface ADR-0028
names as mode identity, that ADR-0142 animates (indigo → violet on trip birth)
and that ADR-0143 is choreographed against; it makes the two theme-fixed screens
above _more_ anomalous, not less; and the backlog already carries a **Hero 2.0**
line for redesigning exactly this region. §5's token contract is what makes it
cheap when it comes.

## Consequences

- **Dark mode becomes shippable.** With §2–§6 it measures **zero failing text
  nodes** across eight routes, against 12 today; light goes from 78 to zero.
- **The light theme changes visibly**, in three tokens and one narrowing. This is
  an accessibility correction with measurements behind each value, not a
  restyle — but it is the first time light mode has moved in a while and it
  should be looked at on a device alongside dark.
- **~100 call sites lose their literal** and gain a token that names its job. Net
  new tokens: 4 on-dark, 2 on-fill, 2 plan-surface, 5 chrome — 13 names replacing
  roughly 24 distinct hex values and 19 hand-written chrome rules.
- **`--faint` stops meaning "one step past muted"** and starts meaning
  "placeholder". Its `design-language.md` entry and every non-placeholder call
  site change with it.
- **Still unverified, and stated as such:** every number here is a Chromium
  render at 411×914. [ADR-0125](0125-map-canvas-terrain-vocabulary.md) is this
  repo's own precedent for a palette that measured fine and read as one hue on
  real glass, and the map epic has had four device corrections of things that
  were derived, tested and wrong. **Phase 6 is the device pass and it is not
  optional.**

## §11 — What the device found, and the hole in the sweep (added phase 5)

The owner ran the shipped dark mode on a real phone before phase 6 and found
three things in minutes. Recording them because **two were invisible to the
audit in §1**, and the reason is instructive.

**1. The active nav tab was dark-on-dark, 1.27:1.** `--nav-accent: var(--indigo)`
— and `--indigo` is a chrome _surface_ token, so it DARKENS on dark. As an accent
on the nav's `--card` ground that is invisible. This is the **third instance** of
this ADR's own §1 shape (after `--plan-deep` and `--amber-deep`): a token whose
value was chosen for one of its two roles. It is now `--ink`, the neutral it
always meant, which flips correctly and is a hair from `--indigo` in light.

**2. The event cards, the settle actions and the maybe shelf never themed.** They
carried hardcoded light _grounds_ — `#f7f7f9`, `#f6faf7`, `#fafbfd`, `#fff`, and
a `repeating-linear-gradient` hatch of `#fff`/`#fbfaf7`. In dark they stayed
white slabs on a dark page.

**This is the hole, and it is a hole in the method, not just the code.** §1's
audit swept **ink** (`color:`) exhaustively and never swept **grounds**
(`background:`) on themeable surfaces. Worse, the runtime contrast sweep
_structurally cannot_ catch it: a light card with dark ink passes contrast
perfectly. It is only wrong relative to the page around it, and contrast is a
local measure. So a sweep that reported "zero failures" was telling the truth
about the question it asked.

The lesson generalises past dark mode: **a contrast audit answers "can you read
it", never "does it belong here".** The second question needs either a ground
sweep or a pair of eyes, and the eyes found it first. A ground sweep now exists
and runs clean, but it was written _after_ the phone.

**3. The map canvas is still the day style.** Predicted and correct — the night
JSON has never been imported in the Cloud console (§10's 👤 step). Confirms the
diagnosis: an unimported Map ID renders Google-default rather than failing.

**And one thing the device found that was never dark mode's:**
`.create-btn:not([data-armed])` dims to 0.45, a rule written for `CreateTrip`'s
submit, which is genuinely not-ready until its form completes (ADR-0150 §8).
`AllTrips` reuses the class for a button that only navigates, never set the
attribute, and had therefore been permanently dim in **both themes** since the
rule landed — sitting next to a real disabled button and reading identically. It
is `frontend/CLAUDE.md`'s own "reusing a component and inheriting its DEFAULTS"
anti-pattern, and it took a theming review to notice.

## §12 — Phase 6, and the second hole in the sweep

Phase 6 was scoped as "look at it on a phone". Looking at it turned up four
things, and **three of them were invisible to the sweep for one shared reason**:
the sweep walked **routes**, and these live in **states**.

**1. `--indigo` as heading ink — 1.10:1 in dark, on `.modal-title`.** Every modal
title in the app, plus the zero state's `h1`, the two `.placeholder` headings and
the document-upload head. `--indigo` is the chrome's ground; used as text it
follows the ground into near-black exactly when the page does. Fourth instance of
§1, and the largest: `.modal-title` is one selector behind every sheet, dialog
and confirm in the app.

**Why the route sweep could not see it.** It visited eight URLs as one seeded
user with trips. That user never opens an overlay and never has zero trips — so
the modal never mounted and the zero state never rendered. **A sweep over routes
is not a sweep over the app.** The static sweep now takes the captured frames
_plus_ a modal and a zero state, which is where these four surfaced.

**2. `--miss` is a fill being read as ink.** `#C2584E` at L\* 50.7 is right for a
dot, a dashed border and the settle mark, and **4.38:1 as text on white** — under
AA at all 37 sites that write with it, in the theme that shipped first. Same
split `--amber`/`--amber-deep` already runs, so: `--miss-deep`, a scalar along
the same RGB ray. **Three call sites converted, 34 left** — each needs its own
ground checked (a `--miss` label on an always-dark surface wants the bright one,
not the deep one), so a blanket rename would be wrong. The backlog carries them.

**3. Plan's nav accent stopped one step short.** Phase 5 corrected the trip nav's
`--indigo`→`--ink` and left `.app[data-mode='plan'] .nav { --nav-accent:
var(--plan) }` alone. An accent read as ink needs the deep variant: bare `--plan`
puts the **active** tab's own label at 4.32:1 in dark.

**4. The identity ramp is fine, and the measurement said otherwise.** §5 keeps an
identity hue from reading as a category pin by **chroma** — the pin is chromatic,
the avatar muted. In dark that margin measures collapsed: `--id-moss` vs
`--cat-leisure` went from 27.6-vs-35.8 to 25.5-vs-**26.2**, ΔE00 6.5, because the
two sets were lifted for the dark board independently, months apart. Rendered at
26/31/44/92px, **it does not reproduce**: the pin is a saturated teardrop on a
canvas, the avatar a muted disc with an initial, and they stay obviously
different. plum/rose, the pair §5 flagged, is 13.4→12.1 and separable at 26px.
The single-ink rule is now **verified rather than asserted**: `#12203A` clears
5.42 minimum in light and 6.61 in dark across all five hues.

No change made. Recorded because the honest outcome of a device pass is
sometimes "the number was scarier than the pixels", and ADR-0125 cuts both ways.

### The chrome went light, which §9 deferred and the owner then asked for

`--chrome-bg` is now the mode's accent at **12% over `--screen`**: trip indigo,
plan violet, so identity rides **hue** where it used to ride luminance. Four
grounds were rendered on the captured DOM; 12%-into-`--screen` won, and
12%-into-white lost by merging with the page — a chrome that does not read as a
band is not chrome.

Three things fell out of it that the deferral had not priced:

- **The dark chrome had the same defect, unnoticed.** `--indigo` #131F38 against
  `--screen` #0F1726 is 4.3 L\* and 1.09:1, with `--card` (L\* 15.7) floating
  _higher_ than the band that carries mode identity. Same 12% answer mixed the
  other way — the accent over `--card` — which restores the plane order. §5's
  "trip chrome is always-dark, so its contract is theme-fixed" is **withdrawn**:
  once light has its own band, the `:root` values are the _light_ chrome and the
  dark block must restate them.
- **A light chrome's ink ramp is tighter than a dark one's.** Four rungs inside
  21 L\*, because the washes are mixed off `--chrome-ink` and therefore _darken_
  the ground beneath the very ink sitting on them. Each rung is the lightest that
  clears 4.5 on the heaviest wash it is actually painted on — 16% for `--mid`,
  8% for `--dim`, 5% for `--num`. One ramp serves both modes: plan's band is the
  lighter, so trip's rungs clear on it.
- **Plan's chrome was the duplication §5 predicted, and it is gone.** Nineteen
  hand-written rules restating `--card`/`--muted`/`--ink` because plan's chrome
  went light in July and re-specified the set by hand. They are now one line —
  plan declares `--chrome-bg` and inherits the rest. The day strip's plan block
  went with them, which is also what fixed the eleven labels that dropped under
  AA the moment the band stopped being white.

**Verified on the captured frames, against `origin/main` on the same frames:**
light **10 → 0** failing text nodes, dark **6 → 0**.

## §10 — The build, in phases

Each phase is independently shippable and independently revertible. Phases 1–3
change **no pixels in light mode** and are pure preparation; the theme only turns
on in phase 4.

Reviewable as a table. |

The night map needs **no map code at all** — `readMapsConfig(env, theme)` already picks the dark Map ID, `documentMapTheme()` already reads `data-theme`, `Map.tsx:514` already latches at mount so a theme flip cannot bill a second map, and the `Dockerfile` already declares the `ARG`. What it does need is a **👤 human Cloud-console step** that no phase can do: importing `waypoint-map-night.json` and associating it with the `waypoint-night` Map ID (`prerequisites-checklist.md` §4, still unticked, **~6h propagation**). Phase 4 is what unblocks the four stalled backlog lines (U-08's dark-mode tail,
ADR-0105's dark boot, ADR-0133's identity-ramp dark pass, and the Phase-6 night
map style). Phase 6 closes them.

## Alternatives considered

- **Mark the ~21 `/login` + `/join` literals `fixed:` and stop there** (this
  session's own first answer). Rejected once the sweep found 53 declarations and
  18 values rather than 21: a marker is a comment asserting intent, where a token
  named `--on-dark-dim` states it and cannot drift. The narrower fix would have
  left the same problem in the board, the chrome, the ticket and the day strip.
- **Give the board an edge in dark mode** (an amber rim, a neutral hairline).
  Both drawn and rejected in the mockup: the amber rim beats the ration by
  spending the ration (an outline is chrome, not time — rule 4), and a _light_
  hairline on the app's _lowest_ plane says "raised", which is the opposite of
  what the board becomes. The board needs no edge, because amber density carries
  it.
- **Store the theme on the user (PATCH /me, `avatarHue`'s precedent).** Rejected
  in §8: it cannot beat the first paint, so it needs a local mirror anyway, and
  then the server copy only adds a post-paint flash.
- **Two rungs instead of three.** Rejected: it forces a shipped default, and a
  dark-mode phone would open light.
- **Darken `--faint` and keep three ink steps.** Rejected in §7 — at AA the third
  step lands 0.6 L\* from the second, so the ramp is a fiction. Narrowing the
  token's meaning is honest where equalising its value is not.
- **Ship the light trip chrome with this.** Rejected in §9 — it is coupled to
  mode identity and two motion set pieces, and belongs with Hero 2.0.
